discussion.title: Treesitter: 'Impossible pattern' query error on Python files (parser/query version mismatch)
discussion.body:
## Symptom

Opening a Python file threw an error from `BufReadPost`/`FileType` autocommands:

```
Query error at 84:3. Impossible pattern:
  (string
   ^
```

Traceback pointed through `vim/treesitter/highlighter.lua` -> `vim/treesitter/query.lua`, triggered from `lua/zayan/plugins/treesitter.lua`.

## Cause

`nvim-treesitter` (`main` branch) updates its bundled query files (`highlights.scm`, etc.) on every plugin update via `git pull`/lazy sync, but installed parser binaries (`parser/<lang>.so`) only get rebuilt when explicitly reinstalled (`:TSUpdate` or `install()`).

In this case the installed `python.so` was compiled **Jul 30**, while the plugin's `queries/python/highlights.scm` had been updated **Aug 1** to target a newer `tree-sitter-python` grammar. The newer query used a pattern (`string` containing `string_content` for docstrings) that the older grammar didn't support, so the query failed to compile — firing on every Python buffer.

## Fix

Reinstall the affected parser so it matches the current queries:

```sh
nvim --headless -c "lua require('nvim-treesitter').install({'python'}, {force = true})" -c "sleep 3" -c "qa"
```

This installs the new parser to `~/.local/share/nvim/site/parser/`, which takes priority on the runtimepath over the stale copy inside the plugin's own directory (`~/.local/share/nvim/lazy/nvim-treesitter/parser/`).

Verified fix with a headless smoke test:

```sh
nvim --headless /tmp/test_ts.py -c "lua local ok,err = pcall(function() vim.treesitter.start(0,'python') end); print('OK:', ok, err)" -c "qa"
```

## Takeaway

If treesitter throws a query/"Impossible pattern" error for a specific language after a plugin update, the installed parser for that language is probably stale relative to the queries — reinstall just that parser rather than debugging the query file.

discussion.title: [Bug] update invokes uv upgrade when the recorded version constraint excludes its target
discussion.body:
## Summary

`ouroboros update` attempts a uv upgrade even when the running installation's receipt contains a root-package version constraint that excludes the selected update target. uv respects the constraint; Ouroboros then reports a package-step success before its version check detects that the package did not advance.

The proposed fix preserves intentional constraints and detects this conflict before package mutation, with actionable recovery guidance. It does not automatically remove pins.

## Impact

Users of version-constrained persistent uv tool installs cannot complete the advertised update through this command. In an existing installation, dependencies changed while Ouroboros remained at 0.55.4; a fresh isolated reproduction had no dependency changes. Both paths ended with an unchanged Ouroboros version and exit code 1. The final stale-version guard works, but runs after the avoidable upgrade attempt and its intermediate success message.

## Environment and evidence

- Windows, uv 0.10.5, CPython 3.13.5.
- Persistent uv tool installation: `ouroboros-ai[mcp]==0.55.4`; selected PyPI target: 0.55.6.
- Explicit environment-local console, `update --yes --runtime none`, with isolated `UV_TOOL_DIR`, `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR`, and cache. No model/provider is required.
- The updater source in 0.55.4, 0.55.6 and current main `f587795674999a09b51530779640730eda55b174` is byte-identical (SHA-256 `39c33c09ac02d18aa65e4ffaf333e750efe6e579059e307ed42601bb41c6a3c3`).
- Also executed the exact current-main `update.py` directly with `runpy.run_path` in that isolated installation (using its real 0.55.4 metadata and receipt, with no version mocks). It exited 1 and stayed at 0.55.4; uv updated an unrelated dependency during this run. The receipt retained `[mcp]` and `==0.55.4`. The real user's receipt and two runtime configuration files were unchanged by both reproductions.

## Steps to reproduce

In a disposable PowerShell session with uv and Python 3.13 installed:

```powershell
$repro = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('ouroboros-pin-repro-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
$env:UV_TOOL_DIR = Join-Path $repro 'tools'
$env:UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR = Join-Path $repro 'bin'
$env:UV_CACHE_DIR = Join-Path $repro 'cache'
$env:PYTHONUTF8 = '1'
uv tool install --python 3.13 --no-python-downloads --no-config --default-index https://pypi.org/simple 'ouroboros-ai[mcp]==0.55.4'
$ooo = Join-Path $env:UV_TOOL_DIR 'ouroboros-ai\Scripts\ouroboros.exe'
& $ooo update --yes --runtime none
$LASTEXITCODE
& $ooo --version
```

This reproduction needs a published target newer than the pinned installation. The target observed here was 0.55.6.

## Expected behavior

Before invoking a package manager, detect that the recorded root-package requirement excludes the selected target. Report the constraint and target, preserve the intentional pin, exit unsuccessfully without package/setup/plugin mutation, and explain how an operator can deliberately revise the constraint while preserving the original uv environment, interpreter, extras, added requirements, and source options.

Only claim that the package was upgraded after verifying the installed version.

## Actual behavior and relevant output

```text
Installed: v0.55.4
Latest:    v0.55.6
Update available: v0.55.4 -> v0.55.6
Installer: uv
Profile: ouroboros-ai==0.55.4
Nothing to upgrade
hint: `ouroboros-ai` is pinned to `0.55.4` (installed with an exact version pin)
Success: Upgraded ouroboros-ai==0.55.4 via uv
Warning: Package upgrade returned success, but the refreshed installation is v0.55.4 (expected at least v0.55.6).
Runtime integration was not refreshed.
```

The receipt still contains `extras = ["mcp"]`; the missing brackets in the rendered profile above are display behavior, not evidence that extras were removed.

[uv documents](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/tools/#upgrading-tools) that tool upgrades retain installation-time version constraints. The updater currently calls `uv tool upgrade <tool_name>` without checking whether its selected target satisfies that constraint.

## Proposed review boundary

- **User problem:** predictable failure and premature success reporting when the uv receipt's root requirement excludes the update target.
- **Supported conditions:** receipt-backed PyPI uv tool installations; active root-package PEP 440 constraints. Unconstrained or target-compatible requirements keep existing behavior.
- **Owner/components:** existing CLI updater and its tests/documentation; a bounded `packaging` runtime dependency for standard specifier/marker handling rather than a custom parser.
- **Non-goals:** automatic unpinning or receipt rewriting, selecting an intermediate version, solving added/transitive package constraints, pipx policy changes, integration recovery, or Windows executable-path repair.
- **Policy:** the intentional constraint remains authoritative. Any later opt-in automatic unpin feature is a separate decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A conflicting uv root requirement is detected before confirmation or package/setup/plugin subprocesses; the receipt and environment are not modified.
- [ ] The diagnostic includes the blocking constraint, selected target, and receipt location, with guidance to deliberately revise only the version requirement while retaining the original manager/root, Python, extras, added requirements and index/options. Do not generate an incomplete reinstall command that silently drops those settings.
- [ ] Exact pins, upper bounds and exclusions that reject the target are blocked; matching ranges/wildcards, inactive markers and unconstrained roots retain normal behavior. Additional packages' version constraints are not interpreted as Ouroboros constraints.
- [ ] `--dry-run` reports the conflict and exits 1 without mutation. `--check` remains the existing version-only, non-mutating query.
- [ ] A package-manager zero exit does not emit an upgrade-success claim before installed-version verification. The existing stale/unverifiable-version failure guard remains.
- [ ] Regression tests cover blocked-path absence of mutations and compatible-path preservation.

## Related work / duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues/PRs for update, exact pins, version constraints, uv receipts and `uv tool upgrade`; no exact duplicate was found as of 2026-10-10.

- #1859 established receipt-preserving updates and the post-upgrade version guard; this proposal keeps that contract.
- #2541 concerns recovery after a successful, version-verified package upgrade and excludes package-manager failures.
- #2536 concerns installed Codex plugin drift; #2066 concerned ephemeral uvx caching.

discussion.title: Compactor delete-request-store initialization fails independently of the main S3 object-store client
discussion.body:
## Problem

In Loki 3.6.11, the main object-store path and the compactor delete-request-store path are initialized separately. In my production setup with an Amazon S3 Express One Zone directory bucket, the main storage client can operate, but the compactor can still fail during delete-request-store initialization when retention is enabled.

The failure I see is:

```text
failed to init delete store: Get "https://<bucket>.s3express-<zone>.<region>.amazonaws.com/?session=": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

## The two client-creation paths

### 1) Main object/data/index client

Loki creates the main object clients here:

- `pkg/loki/modules.go:1670-1681` builds the per-period object clients with `storage.NewObjectClient(periodConfig.ObjectType, "compactor", ...)`
- `pkg/storage/factory.go:658-709` routes S3 backends to `aws.NewS3ObjectClient(...)`
- `pkg/storage/chunk/client/aws/s3_storage_client.go:176-255` builds the AWS S3 client and applies `http_config.ca_file` to the HTTP transport

### 2) Compactor delete-request-store client

The delete-store client is created separately here:

- `pkg/loki/modules.go:1684-1690` builds `storage.NewObjectClient(deleteStore, "delete-store", ...)`
- `pkg/loki/modules.go:1696-1700` passes that client into the compactor
- `pkg/compactor/compactor.go:212-219` immediately initializes delete handling when `retention_enabled` is true
- `pkg/compactor/compactor.go:315-336` wires the delete-request store into the deletion manager

## Why this matters

The compactor startup path touches the delete-request-store immediately when retention is enabled, so any TLS / trust-store mismatch on that path prevents the backend from starting even though the main object-store path is a separate client and may otherwise behave differently at runtime.

In practice this is painful for S3 Express because the failure happens during the `CreateSession`/session bootstrap path for the directory bucket, and the pod can look like it is failing only at startup rather than during ordinary reads/writes.

## Expected behavior

The delete-request-store client should inherit the same S3 TLS trust configuration as the main object-store client, or Loki should expose a clear, documented way to configure the CA bundle for that path as well.

## Suggested fix

Please review whether the delete-request-store initialization path is missing parity with the main object-store path for custom TLS trust / CA bundle handling, especially for S3 Express directory buckets.

discussion.title: eval sandbox is bypassable, and painter-project tools advertise sync but dispatch async
discussion.body:
Found during an autonomous multi-agent evaluation of DCC-MCP: an AI agent built the same hard-surface asset (an attack-helicopter model) to one shared spec in Houdini 22, Maya 2024, Blender 5.2 and 3ds Max 2024 driven only through `dcc-mcp-cli`, then bound Substance Designer PBR maps, rendered a lookdev turntable and stills per DCC. All local paths in this report are redacted.

This issue groups **2 closely-related findings**.

### dcc_introspect__eval 'read-only sandbox' is trivially bypassable to run arbitrary mutating code

**Tool:** `dcc_introspect__eval`  
**Severity (as observed):** suggestion  
**Versions:** dcc-mcp-substance3d-painter 0.1.3, Painter 12.0.1

**Observed**

```
Guard is a naive source-substring check ('__import__','=','import') over eval() with globals {'__builtins__': __builtins__} where __builtins__ is the full dict. Bypass: __builtins__['ex'+'ec'](open(r'...py').read()) runs an arbitrary multi-statement file. A read-only introspection tool must not expose full builtins to eval().
```

**Reproduce**

```
Call dcc_introspect__eval with expression __builtins__['ex'+'ec']('<mutating code>') — it executes despite the read-only claim.
```

### painter-project tools advertise execution:sync but dispatch as async jobs requiring --wait/poll

**Tool:** `painter_project__inspect_project`  
**Severity (as observed):** suggestion  
**Versions:** dcc-mcp-substance3d-painter 0.1.3, Painter 12.0.1

**Observed**

```
inspect_project (and peers) carry metadata execution:sync, timeoutHintSecs:15, but a plain call returns {job_id, status:'pending'} with no result; the result only comes back via --wait (jobs_get_status). The sync/async contract is inconsistent and a naive single call yields nothing.
```

**Reproduce**

```
call painter_project__inspect_project {} without --wait -> {job_id, status:pending}; same WITH --wait -> completed result.
```

---

_Reported from an automated DCC-MCP evaluation run._

discussion.title: HTTP Surfaces: declarative routes with arbitrary request and response serialization
discussion.body:
Umbrella: #357

Stage: HTTP release

Depends on: #882

## Outcome
Expose typed application operations at custom HTTP routes, independently of JSON and independently of the portable UI IR.

This is the HTTP realization of #357: an external participant supplies requests and consumes responses in its own protocol. Jess declares the command/query mapping; the target handles web-server, routing and representation plumbing.

## Scope
- Register methods/routes at startup, including typed path/query/header/body inputs. Detect route collisions with custom and generated routes before serving traffic.
- Request decoding and response encoding are independent extension points. Supply JSON, URL-encoded forms, text and binary examples; allow application/package codecs such as XML, multipart and provider formats.
- Supply a safe multipart path with bounded file/body handling through existing upload capabilities rather than an unbounded in-memory convention.
- Responses explicitly declare status, headers, content type and either buffered or streaming bodies. Support HTML fragments/full documents, redirects, empty responses and binary downloads.
- Allow a fixed representation per route or explicitly declared content negotiation; define unsupported-media and unacceptable-representation outcomes.
- Preserve raw request bytes where verification needs them. Apply resource limits before application decoding; authenticate/verify before domain mapping or dispatch.
- Reuse existing middleware for logging, limits, metrics and authorization. No separate router stack with different security defaults.
- Map structured application outcomes to declared HTTP responses. Input decoding checks structure; commands validate the domain.
- Derive OpenAPI from declared input/response variants and schema metadata where representable. Do not infer schemas by executing arbitrary encoders or assume every body is JSON.
- Honor existing browser security mechanisms for cookie-authenticated writes, including CSRF policy; support explicit CORS configuration for separately hosted clients.
- Stream cancellation and errors after headers are sent have explicit lifecycle semantics.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Route-level tests cover path/query/header/body decoding and startup collisions.
- [ ] A form request invokes a command and receives HTML; a binary route preserves exact bytes/content type.
- [ ] An application-defined non-JSON codec can be registered without changing framework internals.
- [ ] Streaming is bounded/cancellable and does not buffer the whole response.
- [ ] 204, redirects, structured errors, 415 and 406 behavior follows the declared contract.
- [ ] Custom and generated routes obey the same authorization and middleware policies.
- [ ] OpenAPI accurately describes status/media variants rather than declaring JSON universally.

## Additional dependencies
Read bindings use #239/#241/#449. Production write behavior requires #858/#859. HTML helpers are #63; webhook specialization is #269. HTMX release proof is #885.

discussion.title: Request: Object Shape (ivar initialization order) check
discussion.body: ## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] In Ruby 3.2+ there's a concept of "object shapes" where the order of initialization of instance variables affects performance of Ruby code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0lg9Y8gj3FI. The short version is that if you have code that looks like this: ```ruby class MyClass ... def foo @foo ||= get_foo end def bar @bar ||= get_bar end end ``` It will generate two different "object shapes" based on which method is called first. The solution is to initialize those values consistently up front ```ruby class MyClass def initialize(...) @foo = nil @bar = nil end # ... end ``` With this updated code, all instances of this class will have the same object shape and it's better for performance. ## Describe the solution you'd like Scan code for ivar creation that's not in an initialize method, verify that somewhere in the code, that same named ivar is also set to nil in an initialize method. I know this gets hairy fast due to the flexability of Ruby, perhaps we make two rules "obviously bad usage" and "very agressive warnings that you might have to disable a lot" and only enable the "obviously bad usage" by default. ## Describe alternatives you've considered Manually scanning. But a lot of people don't know about it. See https://github.com/puma/puma/pull/3714 for an IRL fix. ## Additional context Robocop meme reference!
discussion.author: schneems

comments.body:
Having some shapes it not such a big deal. It only gets somewhat troublesome if you have too many (currently 8). Consider this benchmark:

```rb
require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile do
  gem 'benchmark-ips'
end

require 'benchmark/ips'

Warning[:performance] = true

class SingleShape
  def initialize(ivar = nil)
    return unless ivar

    create_random_ivars
    instance_variable_set(ivar, 123)
  end

  def create_random_ivars
    (1..10).to_a.shuffle.each { instance_variable_set("@ivar#{it}", 123) }
  end

  def access
    @foo
    @foo
    @foo
    @foo
    @foo
    @foo
    @foo
    @foo
    @foo
    @foo
  end
end

class FiveShapes < SingleShape
end

class TooComplex < SingleShape
end

5.times { FiveShapes.new.create_random_ivars }
15.times { TooComplex.new.create_random_ivars }

# Create an instance with instance variable foo. The benchmark will access it repeatedly
single = SingleShape.new(:@foo)
five = FiveShapes.new(:@foo)
too_complex = TooComplex.new(:@foo)

Benchmark.ips do |x|
  x.report('1') { single.access }
  x.report('5') { five.access }
  x.report('8+') { too_complex.access }
  x.compare!
end
```

Only one class gets the performance penalty:

```rb
test.rb:20: warning: The class TooComplex reached 8 shape variations, instance variables accesses will be slower and memory usage increased.
It is recommended to define instance variables in a consistent order, for instance by eagerly defining them all in the #initialize method.
ruby 3.4.3 (2025-04-14 revision d0b7e5b6a0) +PRISM [x86_64-linux]
Warming up --------------------------------------
                   1     2.227M i/100ms
                   5     2.218M i/100ms
                  8+     1.947M i/100ms
Calculating -------------------------------------
                   1     21.923M (± 0.9%) i/s   (45.61 ns/i) -    111.354M in   5.079777s
                   5     21.949M (± 0.7%) i/s   (45.56 ns/i) -    110.918M in   5.053766s
                  8+     19.113M (± 1.8%) i/s   (52.32 ns/i) -     97.366M in   5.095955s

Comparison:
                   5: 21948791.2 i/s
                   1: 21923011.1 i/s - same-ish: difference falls within error
                  8+: 19113198.0 i/s - 1.15x  slower
```

With JIT enabled, the penality is a bit higher at ~1.45x slower, so that benefits more from fewer shapes.

I think the warning from Ruby with `Warning[:performance] = true` (you have to explicitly enable those, `-W` doesn't cut it) is a better solution. It also considers all the funny ways you can set ivars via metaprogramming (or simply in another file) that rubocop has no chance of knowing about.

discussion.title: Share VS Code installation and Python/Jupyter extension setup across recipes
discussion.body:
Priority: Medium. Work package: WP8.

## Problem and evidence

`code`, `esilpd`, `mne`, and `nipype` repeat editor installation and the same five Python/Jupyter extension installation commands. Examples are [recipes/code/build.yaml:130](https://github.com/neurodesk/neurocontainers/blob/6dda2d2b66d4393dc8e8f32fc51b25baf103720d/recipes/code/build.yaml#L130), [recipes/mne/build.yaml:58](https://github.com/neurodesk/neurocontainers/blob/6dda2d2b66d4393dc8e8f32fc51b25baf103720d/recipes/mne/build.yaml#L58), and [recipes/nipype/build.yaml:152](https://github.com/neurodesk/neurocontainers/blob/6dda2d2b66d4393dc8e8f32fc51b25baf103720d/recipes/nipype/build.yaml#L152).

The launcher behavior currently differs: code forwards arguments with `exec`, while the wrappers in the other consumers do not have equivalent behavior. Deduplicating wrappers without deciding their contract would change user-visible behavior accidentally.

## Scope and implementation guidance

1. Extract a focused editor installation/extension fragment with explicit version/artifact inputs and an optional additional-extension list.
2. Preserve each recipe's editor version, digest, architecture support, base package assumptions, deployment entries, and update-source ownership.
3. Install build assets through declared files and `get_file`. Keep runtime extension assets in paths available without the container home directory.
4. Specify the launcher contract separately: argument forwarding, process replacement/signals, extension lookup, environment initialization, and handling of root/sandbox flags where currently needed.
5. Share wrappers only where their runtime contract matches; retain genuine consumer-specific launch behavior.
6. Migrate all four recipes and remove the common setup duplication. Ensure macro assets participate in change detection/fingerprints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The common five-extension setup has one implementation used by all four consumers.
- [ ] Recipe-specific editor pins and extra extensions remain explicit.
- [ ] The editor launches with required extensions when `/home` is unavailable.
- [ ] Argument forwarding and process behavior are documented and tested for changed wrappers.
- [ ] Existing launcher/module/desktop entry paths remain usable.
- [ ] Shared setup changes select all consumers and invalidate their fingerprints.

## Validation

Validate/regenerate all four recipes and audit updater policies. Build representative affected candidates and run their focused fulltests. Verify installed editor version and extension inventory, wrapper argument forwarding, and a launch smoke check suitable for CI. Use a temporary executable stub to test wrapper arguments/process behavior where a GUI is unnecessary.

## Audit baseline

Findings refer to commit `6dda2d2b66d4393dc8e8f32fc51b25baf103720d`. The audit was read-only and used reference searches, AST inspection, helper SHA-256 comparisons, temporary behavior reproductions, and successful Dockerfile generation for all 83 template-consuming recipes on default x86_64 settings. Container builds/runtime tests were not performed during the audit; the validation above is work to complete with the implementation. Recheck counts and callers against the implementation branch.

discussion.title: Request path stored with altered percent-encoding (HTTP/2 double-escaped, HTTP/1 decoded), and HTTP/1 resend sends a different path
discussion.body:
**Version:** v0.19.1 (0660409), macOS arm64. Same code on `main` (ee2f1c0). Separate from #135 and #136.

### Symptom

Bytes forwarded upstream are correct. What is recorded is not, and an HTTP/1 resend rebuilds the request from that recorded form.

I used a local HTTPS server that echoes the raw request target (hypercorn, ASGI `scope["raw_path"]`), a proxy started with `-insecure`, and this path:

```
/check_uuid/https%3A%2F%2Fsync.example%2Fsetuid%3Fa%3D1?q=x%3Ay
```

| | HTTP/2 | HTTP/1.1 |
|---|---|---|
| received by the server through the proxy | exact | exact |
| `url` stored in the flow | `/check_uuid/https%253A%252F%252Fsync.example%252Fsetuid%253Fa%253D1` | `/check_uuid/https://sync.example/setuid%3Fa=1` |
| received by the server after `resend_http flow_id=…` | exact | `/check_uuid/https://sync.example/setuid` (the decoded `%3F` became the query delimiter) |

So `query` shows a URL the client never sent. For HTTP/1, the decoded `%2F` and `%3F` change which resource the path names, and resending the flow sends a different request. The query string is never affected.

I found it by matching flows against Chrome DevTools Protocol events, which carry the URL as the browser sent it. Ad-tech cookie-sync URLs (`…/check_uuid/https%3A%2F%2F…`) are where it shows up in real traffic.

### Cause

`HTTPMessage.Path` does not have the same meaning in both layers:

- HTTP/2: the `:path` pseudo-header, in wire form (percent-encoding preserved).
- HTTP/1: `parseRequestURI` in `internal/layer/http1/channel.go` returns `u.Path` from `url.ParseRequestURI`, which is the decoded form.

Then `envelopeToFlow` in `internal/pipeline/record_step.go` builds `&url.URL{Path: m.Path, …}`. `String()` escapes `Path`:

- HTTP/2: the wire form is escaped a second time (`%3A` → `%253A`).
- HTTP/1: the decoded form is re-escaped with the default rules, which do not escape `:` or `/`, so the original encoding is lost.

On resend, `resend_http_helpers.go` takes `sendFlow.URL.Path`, the decoded form. HTTP/2 comes back right only because decoding once undoes the double escape. The HTTP/1 wire encoder (`wireencode.go`) writes `msg.Path` verbatim into the request line, so the decoded `?` splits the target.

### Fix tried locally

Keep `Path` in wire form everywhere and convert to and from `net/url` in exactly one place (`Path` for the decoded form, `RawPath` for the wire bytes):

- New `internal/envelope/wirepath.go`:
  - `URLFromWirePath(scheme, host, wirePath, rawQuery)` sets `Path` to the unescaped form and `RawPath` to the wire bytes, so `String()` returns the wire bytes unchanged.
  - `WirePath(u)` returns `RawPath` while it still encodes `Path`, otherwise `EscapedPath()`. It therefore stays correct after a consumer rewrites `Path`, as the fuzzer does.
- `parseRequestURI` returns `envelope.WirePath(u)` instead of `u.Path`.
- These call sites now use the helpers instead of building `url.URL{Path: …}` or reading `URL.Path`:
  - `record_step.go` (HTTP and gRPC branches);
  - `resend_http_helpers.go` (path inherited from the flow, scope URL);
  - `resend_ws_helpers.go` and `fuzz_ws_helpers.go` (upgrade path);
  - `job/http_source.go` and `job/fuzz_http_source.go`.

With that change, all six cells of the table above are exact. Tests that fail without the change:

- `TestParseRequestURI`, with three encoded cases added;
- `TestRecordStep_FlowURLKeepsWirePathEncoding`;
- `TestURLFromWirePathRoundTrip`, which covers `String()` → `url.Parse` → `WirePath`, the round trip the flow store does.

`go test -race` passes on cmd, envelope, pipeline, layer/http1, layer/http2, mcp, job and flow.

I can share the diff if it helps.

Thanks!

- New `internal/envelope/wirepath.go`:

  - `WirePath(u)` returns `RawPath` while it still encodes `Path`, otherwise `EscapedPath()`. It therefore stays correct after a consumer rewrites `Path`, as the fuzzer does.
- `parseRequestURI` returns `envelope.WirePath(u)` instead of `u.Path`.

  - `record_step.go` (HTTP and gRPC branches);
  - `resend_http_helpers.go` (path inherited from the flow, scope URL);
  - `resend_ws_helpers.go` and `fuzz_ws_helpers.go` (upgrade path);
  - `job/http_source.go` and `job/fuzz_http_source.go`.

- `TestParseRequestURI`, with three encoded cases added;
- `TestRecordStep_FlowURLKeepsWirePathEncoding`;
- `TestURLFromWirePathRoundTrip`, which covers `String()` → `url.Parse` → `WirePath`, the round trip the flow store does.

discussion.title: Wrapping the first line of a multiline Python docstring
discussion.body:
Greetings! First off, thank you for this extension, it's awesome and I use it on a daily basis. There's a situation I routinely run into with Python that breaks and needs to be fixed manually.

```python
"""I have a docstring that starts like this and spans multiple lines and I want to reflow the first line so it wraps correctly.

Docstring continues...
"""
```

If I select the entire first line (by clicking the line number in the gutter) and hit Alt+Q to rewrap it:

```python
"""I have a docstring that starts like this and spans multiple lines and I want to reflow the first
"""line so it wraps correctly.

Docstring continues...
"""
```

I have to remove the quotes it added on the next line. I think it's assuming it should be a single-line docstring and trying to close it.

I spent a few hours today to see if I could adjust the Python parser but ultimately had to admit defeat. I don't know F# but it seems like it could be related to how the regex capture groups handle docstrings, or it could be something in blockComment's overall processing.

It would be wonderfully helpful if this kind of docstring formatting could be supported and I really appreciate any time spent looking into it. Happy to help or test if needed.

discussion.title: Line wrapping in .po files does not match gettext line wrapping
discussion.body:
It looks like the line wrapping we apply to .po files is slightly different from what gettext does:
1. We only wrap `msgstr` contents, and long `msgid` values are left unwrapped.
2. We're ok wrapping immediately before a space, and not just right after it like gettext does.

Internally, we use `polib` for this, so to some extent this is caused by izimobil/polib#96 and this issue is just a pointer onwards, but given these divergences maybe we'd like to update the default value in https://github.com/mozilla/moz-l10n/blob/b8626e45519630b4a42a34daaf507f76c7e1e5c8/python/moz/l10n/formats/gettext/serialize.py#L26-L32 to something much larger to hit this issue less. We're already defaulting to something different than gettext due to internal Mozilla historical reasons, so defaulting to something different would not be that great a change.

discussion.title: AI chat safeguards: off-topic use, prompt injection and forged context
discussion.body:
## Summary
The student chat (`/api/chat/report`) is supposed to answer only about the student's lab. The only thing enforcing that today is one sentence in the system prompt ([`src/narrative.py#L184-L195`](https://github.com/Aldrinerd/Netgrader/blob/1a3d747be3de281626a82a2e2140d5fd1080f12a/src/narrative.py#L184-L195)). On a 3B local model that is easy to get around. A student can use the lab's AI as a general chatbot, ask it to write essays or other coursework, or get the full fixing configuration the prompt tells it to withhold.

## Specific weaknesses
1. **Off-topic scope is prompt-only.** Nothing checks the question, or the answer, against the lab's subject matter.
2. **The client supplies the grounding.** The endpoint accepts `report` from the browser. A student can send a crafted report whose `description`, `feedback` or `actual_value` fields contain instructions ("ignore previous rules…"). Those fields are pasted into the model's context as trusted findings.
3. **Forged assistant turns.** `clean_chat_messages` accepts `assistant` messages from the client, so a student can plant fake prior replies ("Sure, here's the full config: …") to steer the model.
4. **No output check.** Replies aren't screened for full configuration blocks, or for content outside networking.
5. **No rate limit.** See the separate model-concurrency issue.

## Proposed approach
- **Server-side grounding:** chat about a *stored* submission by ID (depends on the submission-database issue), never about a client-supplied report. Until then, re-validate the report and strip or escape free-text fields.
- **Topic gate before the model:**
  - a cheap deterministic check (networking keyword and lab-entity match against the report's devices and interfaces), plus
  - a short classifier call ("Is this about computer networking or this lab? yes/no").
  - Off-topic → fixed refusal. The main model is never called.
- **History integrity:** keep the conversation server-side keyed by session, or HMAC-sign assistant turns so forged ones are rejected.
- **Output filter:**
  - reject or trim replies containing more than N consecutive IOS config lines;
  - run the same topic check on the answer.
- **Instructor visibility:** chat transcripts (per submission) visible to the instructor, with a notice shown to students.
- **Prompt hardening:** delimit findings as data, and state that instructions inside the findings must be ignored.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Red-team test set in `tests/` (off-topic requests, injected report fields, forged assistant turns, "write the whole config"), and every case is refused or handled.
- [ ] Refusals are deterministic (template text, `source: "template"`), not model-written.
- [ ] Legitimate lab questions still answered (no over-blocking on the existing chat tests).

discussion.title: agentic-governance: untrusted tool results bypass injection filtering before model context
discussion.body:
## Finding

ADR-043 identifies scraped web/OSINT content as a primary indirect-prompt-injection distribution and describes agentic-loop routing tool results through governance. Current agentic-governance inputs are only `agent.task.*`, `agent.request.*`, and `agent.response.*`; `HandleToolResult` instead converts result content directly into a role=`tool` message and sends it in the next model request.

Evidence at `origin/main` `ad153b2000d2f1797fcba7446ed2a324ca546d35`:

- intended threat/flow: `docs/adr/043-prompt-injection-defense-detonation-corpus.md:9-47,210-220`
- current governance inputs: `processor/agentic-governance/config.go:185-219`; `processor/agentic-governance/component.go:308-337`
- direct tool-result context path: `processor/agentic-loop/handlers.go:2111-2181,2423-2478,2528-2570`
- full pre-truncation trajectory evidence: `processor/agentic-loop/handlers.go:2117,2130-2147`; `processor/agentic-loop/trajectory_evidence.go:22-96`

## Boundary

This issue owns classification/admission of untrusted result content before model consumption.

- #1045 separately owns making an already-produced governance verdict decodable and rule-readable; its three barriers do not create the missing `tool.result.*` ingestion path.
- #1049 owns preventing rule action templates from emitting opaque governance values; it matters only if disposition is rule-driven.
- #1058 owns booted E2E proof for the RuleReadable projection path if that path is claimed.
- #1033 shares the result-truncation seam; this issue must not re-derive truncation independently.
- #808 owns effect-derived approval of tool calls, not returned-content classification.
- #1006 owns non-Go dereference and authorization for stored evidence.
- #857 owns the systemic payload-size class and constrains any new result carrier.
- #1113 owns booted-binary E2E proof of existing web-observation entity birth.

#1045, #1049, and #1058 constrain a design that sends governance dispositions through rules. They do not block an inline classify/redact/block path before model context.

## Owner decisions required

- Whether governance blocks, redacts, annotates, or quarantines result content, and how shadow mode behaves.
- Whether the governed carrier is the existing result message, a derived bounded view, or another admitted contract.
- How full durable trajectory evidence is retained/access-controlled when model-visible content is altered or rejected.

## Acceptance

- Every external-content-producing builtin (`http_request`, `web_search`, bash URL fetches, and any future renderer) has a tested result-content governance path before model context.
- Missing/unavailable required governance fails closed or produces an explicit typed degraded state; it is not silent.
- Provenance and remote-content delimiters survive truncation/redaction.
- The solution preserves immutable completed tool outcomes and does not duplicate the adjacent owners listed above.

Owner accepted capturing this finding on 2026-08-27; detailed policy semantics remain `status:needs-decision`.
discussion.author: cglusky

comments.body:
OWNER RULING — APPROVED (2026-08-28)

Proceed with the tool-result governance design under these boundaries:

- Governance is optional through an explicit `disabled | shadow | enforce` mode. Disabled mode has no governance dependency.
- Policy selection is configuration-driven through named, versioned profiles. Mode controls disposition; profile controls classifiers, thresholds, corpus, redaction, and evaluation order.
- The first slice admits measured built-in profiles behind that stable seam. Arbitrary operator-authored policy definitions and per-tool bypass/exemption rules are deferred until corpus measurement justifies and bounds them.
- Unknown or unavailable non-disabled profiles fail explicitly at boot; there is no silent fallback.
- Governance applies consistently to every nonterminal external-content result before it enters model context, independent of tool name or effect declaration.
- Immutable raw completed outcomes and trajectory evidence remain intact; governance alters only the bounded model-visible copy.
- Shadow mode records the same decision without changing the model-visible content. Enforce mode applies the selected profile disposition.
- Do not introduce a new payload, stream, quarantine store, or general policy DSL merely for this slice.
- Terminal tool output that does not become a role=`tool` model input remains outside this issue.

The implementation must still pass the project architecture/reviewer gates, including restart, duplicate-delivery, correlation-key, and terminalization safety. This ruling settles product semantics; it does not waive those correctness requirements.

comments.body:
BLOCKER UPDATE — framework restart safety

The owner-approved ToolResult governance semantics remain binding: optional disabled/shadow/enforce mode, named/versioned built-in profiles, immutable raw evidence, and governance of the bounded model-visible copy.

Architecture review of approval-result correlation exposed a pre-existing critical framework defect now owned by #1146: agentic-loop persists `LoopEntity` but does not hydrate/reconcile its process-only context and correlation state after replacement, while several durable-input handlers ACK missing-state paths. The broader legibility/conformance contract is tracked by #1145 under epic #1147.

#1140 must not solve that systemic defect by inventing a private approval transaction manager, generic checkpoint bucket, or CQRS/event-replay path. Its independently valid classifier/profile/framing work survives, but enforcement, approval-pause recovery, and any restart-safety claim are blocked on #1146.

Blocked by: #1146.
